title: Ocean Conservation Fund and the intermediary philanthropy landscape
summary: Five connected, fictional scenarios: a direct grant followed end to end, and four ways funding can flow through intermediaries -- fiscal sponsorship, a donor-advised fund, regranting, and a collaborative fund -- showing the same core organization occupying multiple independently-dated roles at once, plus the other organizations that connect around it.

individuals.label: Ocean Conservation Fund
individuals.narrative: The Ocean Conservation Fund (fictional) is a foundation that funds marine habitat restoration work.

individuals.label: Marine Habitat Protection Program
individuals.narrative: It maintains a standing Marine Habitat Protection Program with a $2,000,000 annual budget.

individuals.label: 2026 Cycle 1
individuals.narrative: The program's first 2026 funding cycle runs January through early March.

individuals.label: 2026 Marine Habitat Protection Grants
individuals.narrative: Within that cycle, the Fund opens a Funding Opportunity with a March 1 deadline.

individuals.label: Coastal Watch Alliance
individuals.narrative: Coastal Watch Alliance (fictional), a coastal-habitat nonprofit, decides to apply.

individuals.label: Coastal Watch Alliance FY26 Application
individuals.narrative: Coastal Watch submits its Application on February 15, proposing a habitat restoration project.

individuals.label: Coastal Watch Alliance FY26 Review
individuals.narrative: Two program staff review the application against the program's Review Criteria.

individuals.label: Coastal Watch Alliance FY26 Decision
individuals.narrative: On March 20, the review results in a Decision to approve the application.

individuals.label: Award to Coastal Watch Alliance
individuals.narrative: The Fund makes a $250,000 Award, effective April 1.

individuals.label: Grant Agreement with Coastal Watch Alliance
individuals.narrative: Both parties sign a Grant Agreement formalizing the award's terms.

individuals.label: Coastal Watch Alliance Payment Schedule
individuals.narrative: The agreement sets a Payment Schedule disbursing the award in four quarterly installments.

individuals.label: Q2 2026 Installment
individuals.narrative: The first Installment, $62,500, is released for Q2 2026.

individuals.label: Q2 2026 Payment
individuals.narrative: The corresponding Payment is sent on April 15.

individuals.label: Coastal Watch Alliance Reporting Schedule
individuals.narrative: The agreement also attaches a quarterly Reporting Schedule.

individuals.label: Coastal Watch Alliance Quarterly Reporting Requirement
individuals.narrative: Timely reporting is a standing Compliance Requirement of the award.

individuals.label: Q2 2026 Narrative & Financial Report
individuals.narrative: Coastal Watch submits its first combined narrative and financial Report on July 10, ahead of the July 15 deadline; the Fund accepts it.

individuals.label: 12 Habitat Restoration Workshops Held
individuals.narrative: By year end, the project has produced a direct Output: 12 habitat restoration workshops held.

individuals.label: Improved Coastal Habitat Health
individuals.narrative: Those workshops contribute to the intended Outcome: measurably improved coastal habitat health.

individuals.label: Year 1 Outcomes Evaluation
individuals.narrative: A Year 1 Evaluation, completed January 15 2027, assesses both the output and the outcome.

individuals.label: Coastal Watch Alliance FY26 Closeout
individuals.narrative: With all payments disbursed and all reports accepted, the award reaches Closeout on February 1, 2027.

individuals.label: Ocean Conservation Fund
individuals.narrative: Ocean Conservation Fund is itself an Organization, not just a Funder -- and it turns out to occupy more than one role. Its Funder occupancy above covers the Coastal Watch Alliance grant; here, in a separate arrangement, it also acts as a Fiscal Sponsor.

individuals.label: Ocean Conservation Fund (as Fiscal Sponsor)
individuals.narrative: This occupancy is a distinct, independently-dated Organization Role from its Funder role above -- effective May 1, 2026, and scoped to a single sponsored project.

individuals.label: Tidewater Youth Ocean Corps Fiscal Sponsorship
individuals.narrative: The two parties formalize a Fiscal Sponsorship Arrangement, under which Ocean Conservation Fund charges an 8% administrative fee on funds it processes on the project's behalf.

individuals.label: Tidewater Youth Ocean Corps
individuals.narrative: Tidewater Youth Ocean Corps (fictional) is a youth-led tide pool restoration group. It isn't independently incorporated, so it operates -- and receives funding -- under Ocean Conservation Fund's fiscal sponsorship.

individuals.label: Pacific Coastal Trust
individuals.narrative: Pacific Coastal Trust (fictional), a separate foundation, wants to fund the project directly but needs a fiscally sponsored recipient it can grant to.

individuals.label: Pacific Coastal Trust Community Grants Fund
individuals.narrative: It grants from its Community Grants Fund, open since 2020.

individuals.label: Award for Tidewater Youth Ocean Corps Restoration Work
individuals.narrative: On May 15, Pacific Coastal Trust makes a $45,000 Award. Because the money is for the sponsored project, the Award's party edges diverge from a direct grant: it's awardedBy Pacific Coastal Trust, awardedTo and managedBy Ocean Conservation Fund (which holds legal responsibility and administers it day to day), and fundedFrom the Community Grants Fund -- while Tidewater Youth Ocean Corps is the intended beneficiary via the Fiscal Sponsorship Arrangement above.

individuals.label: Alvarez Family Fund
individuals.narrative: Ocean Conservation Fund also sponsors the Alvarez Family Fund (fictional), a Donor-Advised Fund it holds and administers on behalf of a family that wants ongoing input into its giving without running its own foundation.

individuals.label: Elena Alvarez
individuals.narrative: Elena Alvarez (fictional), the fund's original donor, is its Donor Advisor -- she can recommend grants and investments, but Ocean Conservation Fund retains legal control over the money.

individuals.label: Alvarez Family Fund Advisory Arrangement
individuals.narrative: The advisory relationship is formalized as a Donor-Advised Fund Arrangement, distinct from Ocean Conservation Fund's Funder and Fiscal Sponsor occupancies above -- a third, independently-dated engagement for the same organization.

individuals.label: Coral Reef Defenders
individuals.narrative: Coral Reef Defenders (fictional) is a marine conservation nonprofit Elena has supported informally for years.

individuals.label: Recommendation to fund Coral Reef Defenders
individuals.narrative: Elena submits a Grant Recommendation asking the fund to support Coral Reef Defenders. It's non-binding by design -- Ocean Conservation Fund still has to approve it -- but in this case it does.

individuals.label: Award to Coral Reef Defenders
individuals.narrative: The recommendation leads to a $15,000 Award. Ocean Conservation Fund awards and administers it, funded from the Alvarez Family Fund rather than its own general grantmaking budget.

individuals.label: National Ocean Legacy Fund
individuals.narrative: National Ocean Legacy Fund (fictional), a larger national foundation, wants to fund grassroots coastal restoration groups but lacks the local relationships to identify them directly.

individuals.label: Ocean Conservation Fund (as Funding Intermediary)
individuals.narrative: It regrants through Ocean Conservation Fund instead -- a fourth, independently-dated role for the same organization: Funding Intermediary, alongside its Funder, Fiscal Sponsor, and Donor-Advised Fund host occupancies.

individuals.label: National Ocean Legacy Regranting Program
individuals.narrative: The relationship is structured as a Regranting Arrangement: Ocean Conservation Fund receives the funds as a subrecipient and redistributes them to smaller groups it already works with.

individuals.label: Award to Ocean Conservation Fund
individuals.narrative: National Ocean Legacy Fund awards Ocean Conservation Fund $200,000 for regranting.

individuals.label: Kelp Forest Collective
individuals.narrative: Kelp Forest Collective (fictional), a small kelp-restoration group, is one of the local organizations Ocean Conservation Fund regrants to.

individuals.label: Sub-grant to Kelp Forest Collective
individuals.narrative: Ocean Conservation Fund -- now acting as the funder rather than the recipient -- awards Kelp Forest Collective a $35,000 sub-grant from that pool.

individuals.label: Tidewater Community Foundation
individuals.narrative: Tidewater Community Foundation (fictional) partners with Pacific Coastal Trust to fund coastal resilience work neither wants to take on alone.

individuals.label: Coastal Resilience Fund
individuals.narrative: The two pool their contributions into the Coastal Resilience Fund, administered by Tidewater Community Foundation.

individuals.label: Coastal Resilience Collaborative
individuals.narrative: Their partnership is a Collaborative Fund Arrangement -- both organizations participate in directing the shared fund's grantmaking.

individuals.label: Coastal Resilience Grant to Kelp Forest Collective
individuals.narrative: The collaborative's first award, $20,000, goes to Kelp Forest Collective -- the same small group Ocean Conservation Fund regrants to, now drawing on a second, independent funding stream.
